assumptions: The flag change at 13:35 UTC is assumed to have been a deliberate human or automated action; no actor, ticket, or change-log entry for it appears in the evidence reviewed.

Causation is inferred from correlation and from the fix working: the error type changed to ZeroDivisionError exactly when the flag went off, and the service returned to baseline when it was turned back on. No code was read and no stack trace was traced to a specific line, so the exact faulty expression in the non-fallback path is unconfirmed.

The low-level UpstreamTimeout errors on the account page before 13:35 are assumed to be pre-existing background noise unrelated to this incident; they were present throughout the preceding half hour and were not investigated.
The partial-rollout minute at 13:35 (a mixed off/on evaluation split) is assumed to reflect the flag propagating across instances rather than a deliberate staged rollout.
The evidence bundle contains the 13:25-13:40 log window twice; this is assumed to be a duplicate of the same records, not two distinct sets of events.
Restoring the flag is a mitigation, not a fix. It is assumed the non-fallback path still carries the defect and will fail the same way if the flag is turned off again.
input.executive_summary: On 12 September 2026, a configuration switch in the shop service was turned off at 13:35 UTC. That switch had been routing customers through an older, working version of the account page; with it off, requests fell through to a newer code path that crashes. From that moment, a substantial and sustained share of attempts to load the account page failed outright, while the rest of the site continued to serve normally. Monitoring raised an alert at 13:40 UTC, about five minutes after the failures began. The automated responder identified the switch as the cause within seconds, but its first proposed fix was blocked by a safety gate because no reversible action had been attached to it; it re-investigated, reached the same conclusion with the supporting evidence attached, and turned the switch back on at 13:42 UTC. Error rates returned to their normal background level immediately. Customer impact was limited to failed account-page loads during that window; no data was lost and no manual engineering intervention was required. The underlying crash in the newer code path has not been fixed — the service is currently healthy only because it is running on the older path again.
input.root_cause: The `legacy-checkout-fallback` feature flag on io-shop was switched off at 13:35 UTC, moving account-page traffic onto the non-fallback rendering path, which contains a latent divide-by-zero bug (`ZeroDivisionError`) and fails for a large share of requests. The flag flip exposed the bug rather than introducing it; the flag had been serving the safe legacy path continuously up to that point, and no deploy is recorded anywhere in the 2026-09-10 to 2026-09-12 change log, which is why the "unrecorded code change" alternative was discarded.
